lvars._comment: Shared Fenix A32x FCU annunciator and parking-brake readbacks. The trusted fenix-a32x adapter owns the larger aircraft-specific field and action surface.

controls._comment: Aircraft-specific cockpit writes are selected only from the trusted fenix-a32x adapter. Persistent switches/selectors retain fixed targets and exact readback. The reviewed FCU subset adds bounded MobiFlight-only press/release pulses, managed push/pull commands, and stepped speed/heading/altitude targets. Four paired forward-throttle detents set and independently confirm both levers; reverse thrust and arbitrary axis values remain excluded along with unrelated momentary, guarded emergency, breaker, maintenance, preset, and macro controls. Standard gear/flap actions remain available on the narrow shared surface.

meta.notes: Shared trusted integration for the Fenix A319, A320, and A321. The adapter exposes 120 live fields, 277 trusted actions, and 119 action-confirmation fields across persistent exterior/cockpit lighting, cabin, electrical, fuel, pneumatic, hydraulic, ADIRS, EFIS, switching, radio, weather-radar, transponder, brake, engine-mode, GPWS, the reviewed FCU subset, and four paired forward-throttle detents. Every write is cooldown-guarded, never retries automatically, and requires exact logical readback.

sources.name: FenixSim Support Hub - binding switches, knobs and buttons
sources.notes: Fenix identifies its shipped Cockpit_Behavior.xml and interaction templates as the authoritative LVar/control source and publicly demonstrates fixed 0/1 writes plus bounded A_*_LIGHTING values. The adapter's I_FCU_*, N_FCU_*, S_*, E_FCU_*, and A_* fields, raw detents, and fixed or bounded write recipes were reviewed against licensed Fenix A320 MSFS 2024 package version 2.4.0.4720: the legacy cockpit file, modular panel *Behavior.xml files, and FNX32X interaction templates. The reviewed FCU contract uses stable I_FCU_AP1/AP2/ATHR/LOC/APPR/EXPED readback for paired S_FCU_* press/release counter increments; I_FCU_SPEED/HEADING/ALTITUDE_MANAGED for S_FCU_SPEED/HEADING/ALTITUDE push (decrement) and pull (increment); and fresh N_FCU_SPEED/HEADING/ALTITUDE baselines for bounded repeated E_FCU_SPEED/HEADING/ALTITUDE increments or decrements. The reviewed throttle template maps A_FC_THROTTLE_LEFT_INPUT and A_FC_THROTTLE_RIGHT_INPUT values 2, 3, 4, and 5 to IDLE, CLB, FLX/MCT, and TOGA; Flight Fabric writes both together and confirms both separately. Reverse positions and continuous axis control are excluded. N_FCU_VS is display-only because its raw value does not identify VS versus FPA mode. S_MIP_PARKING_BRAKE uses 0=released and 1=set; S_FCU_EFIS*_BARO_MODE uses 0=INHG and 1=HPA; S_FCU_ALTITUDE_SCALE uses 0=1000 ft and 1=100 ft.

sources.name: Fenix A319 and A321 Expansion
sources.notes: Confirms the supported A319 and A321 family variants and their shared family development baseline. Variant-only controls still fail closed when their live LVar is unavailable; the page hides A319/A320 center-pump and pack-flow controls on A321 and shows the ACT control only on A321.

sources.name: Fenix A320 V2 Block 2 release
sources.notes: Documents Fenix's expanded hardware LVar and internal input-event work. This adapter uses only source-audited persistent or bounded LVar counter contracts and does not assume custom InputEvents are executable.

sources.name: MSFS 2024 SimConnect Input Events
sources.notes: Documents native Input Event discovery/read/write support. The adapter can add proven Input Event routes later; current Fenix writes use its vendor-documented LVar interaction contract.

knownIssues: The expanded write routes were audited against a current licensed A320 package but still require live in-simulator validation before being promoted from untested.
A319 and A321 matching and common/variant LVar compatibility require live validation with the expansion installed.
The A321 uses ECON FLOW in place of the A319/A320 pack-flow selector; the shared template hides the A319/A320 pack-flow readout for the A321 profile.
The new AP1/AP2, A/THR, LOC, APPR, EXPED, managed push/pull, and speed/heading/altitude target actions are source-audited but remain untested in the live aircraft.
The paired IDLE, CLB, FLX/MCT, and TOGA throttle targets are source-audited and backend-tested but remain untested in the live aircraft; reverse thrust and arbitrary axis values are excluded.

A numeric FCU target can require hundreds of calculator increments from a fresh baseline. The bounded route stops on the first failed acknowledgement or profile-generation change and never retries, so an interrupted sequence can leave an intermediate target.
N_FCU_VS is exposed for display only; no vertical target action is enabled because the raw value is ambiguous between VS and FPA mode.
Logical readback proves the vendor LVar reached its fixed target; it does not independently prove every downstream aircraft-system effect.
